title: Slabless memory fabric: dynamic weight/KV/activation budgeting for continuous batching
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Continuous batching workloads with varied sequence-length distributions cause unpredictable pressure across three memory pools (weights, KV cache, activations). Current slab-based allocation creates fragmentation and large static headroom that inflates costs and forces conservative throttling decisions.

Goal: Implement a 'slabless memory fabric' — a cooperative, lease-driven budgeting layer that treats weights, KV, and activations as soft-capacity bands with dynamic transfers and a small probabilistic reserve for microbursts. The fabric should: (1) reduce steady-state headroom by at least 25% for mixed sequence workloads, (2) keep P99 token latency regressions < 5% vs baseline, and (3) provide clear accounting for per-tenant billing and debugging.

Approach: Replace rigid slab boundaries with a lightweight ledger that tracks alloc/delta events and computes three derived signals in realtime: residual_budget (per-GPU global), marginal_eviction_curve (per-tenant KV/activation elasticity), and predictive_reserve (short-horizon headroom from continuous-batching forecasts). The runtime will use these signals to: 1) prefer transient activation over immediate KV spill when a predicted sequence tail will reuse the KV; 2) softly borrow from weight-anchored buffer using quantization-aware sketches for pinned model shards during sustained bursts; and 3) expose a telemetry surface that surfaces marginal unit cost (tokens/MB) so the Console can show per-route tradeoffs.
implementation_notes:
Phase 1 (prototype, feature-flagged): implement lightweight ledger with O(1) update hook in allocator; add estimator for marginal_eviction_curve using EWMA of reuse probability; integrate short-horizon predictor (30s sliding window) derived from Batcher windows. Phase 2: integrate with KV prefetch hints and quantization advisor; experiment with temporary weight pinning via compressed shadow weights. Phase 3: rollout with canary on dedicated pools, add cost-modeling dashboard.

Instrumentation: add counters for borrow events, eviction_count_by_reason, predicted_vs_actual_headroom, and per-tenant marginal_cost samples. Telemetry will be exported to Prometheus and a backend timeseries for Console graphs.

Operational controls: feature flag 'slabless_fabric_v1', adjustable parameters: reserve_quantile (default 0.99), max_borrow_fraction (default 0.12), ewma_alpha, and forecast_window_seconds.

Performance budget: ensure allocator path adds < 3us median per-request overhead and < 12us P99 on our stressbed (A100-like).
acceptance_criteria: Prototype ledger implements O(1) update hook and passes unit tests for concurrent alloc/dealloc
End-to-end canary shows >=25% reduction in configured steady-state headroom on mixed-length benchmark (short+long tails)
P99 token latency regression <=5% vs current slab allocator under 95th percentile load
Console telemetry surfaces marginal_cost metric and a per-tenant borrow/evict timeline
Runtime feature flag and per-pool toggle exist; rollout playbook documented
risks: Risk of oscillation between KV and activation borrowing under highly bursty tenants; mitigated by conservative max_borrow_fraction and hysteresis on predictor. Risk that compressed weight pinning increases GPU memory churn — will gate behind quantization advisor and only enable after latency regression tests pass. Requires careful cross-check with billing pipeline to avoid inconsistent per-tenant accounting during borrows.
